domain: Transportation Systems / Social Coordination / Path Dependence
topic_summary: Analysis of the convention determining which side of the road vehicles drive on, examining the coordination mechanism that stabilizes right-hand driving in most jurisdictions and left-hand driving in others. The topic encompasses the physical infrastructure lock-in, network effects of standardization, and the historical path dependence that created the current global distribution.

key_entities: Right-hand traffic jurisdictions (majority of world by land area and population)
Left-hand traffic jurisdictions (UK, Japan, Australia, India, former British colonies)
Vehicle manufacturers (design steering wheel placement and control orientation)
Border crossing infrastructure (transition zones between different-handedness jurisdictions)
Historical precedent actors (Napoleon's military standardization, British Empire colonial policy)
key_tensions: Coordination benefit of global standardization vs cost of transition for established systems
Network externality (value increases with adoption) vs infrastructure sunk costs

axes.human_readable: Coordination Equilibrium Selection (Which Side Becomes Standard)
axes.structural_delta: The mechanism by which one of two equivalent coordination equilibria (left vs right) becomes locally stable
axes.primary_observable: Geographic distribution of handedness adoption; historical timing of standardization decisions
axes.selection_reason: Upstream coordination mechanism; structurally distinct from physical infrastructure and distinct observable from network effects

axes.structural_delta: The accumulated physical infrastructure (road design, signage, vehicle fleet) that makes switching prohibitively expensive
axes.primary_observable: Capital stock value of handedness-specific infrastructure; estimated transition costs for jurisdiction switching
axes.selection_reason: Different observable (physical capital vs coordination mechanism); mountain hypothesis distinct from rope; passes independence test

axes.human_readable: Network Externality Gradient (Value Scales with Adoption)
axes.structural_delta: The increasing coordination value as more jurisdictions adopt the same handedness standard
axes.primary_observable: Trade volume and cross-border traffic flow between same-handedness vs different-handedness jurisdiction pairs
axes.selection_reason: Different observable from coordination_equilibrium_selection (adoption value vs selection mechanism) and infrastructure_lock_in (network effects vs sunk costs); passes independence test

axes.structural_delta: The operational costs and safety risks at borders between different-handedness jurisdictions
axes.primary_observable: Accident rates at handedness-transition borders; infrastructure costs of transition zones
axes.selection_reason: Downstream synthesis node; different observable (border transition costs vs either coordination or infrastructure); tangled_rope with identifiable beneficiary/victim structure

axes.human_readable: Cognitive Handedness Bias (Right-Hand Dominance in Population)
axes.structural_delta: The hypothesis that right-hand traffic aligns with right-hand dominance in human population
axes.primary_observable: Population handedness distribution; ergonomic studies of control placement preference
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: speculative biological determinism; no strong evidence that handedness distribution drove convention selection; zero centrality; omega material

axes.human_readable: Military Standardization Legacy (Napoleonic and Colonial Imposition)
axes.structural_delta: The historical mechanism by which military conquest imposed handedness standards
axes.primary_observable: Correlation between Napoleonic conquest territories and right-hand traffic; British colonial territories and left-hand traffic
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: historical mechanism already captured in coordination_equilibrium_selection's path dependence; scaffold provides context but not independent structural delta

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Hypothesis that right-hand traffic aligns with population handedness distribution
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Speculative biological determinism with weak empirical support; zero graph centrality; no evidence handedness distribution drove convention selection

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Historical military conquest as handedness imposition mechanism
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Historical context already captured in coordination_equilibrium_selection path dependence; scaffold provides narrative but not independent structural constraint

omegas.description: Sweden's 1967 Dagen H transition from left to right demonstrates infrastructure_lock_in is surmountable but at extraordinary cost. Does this reclassify the mountain as a piton of political will rather than physical necessity?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - successful transition case not addressed in initial framing

omegas.description: Do autonomous vehicles eliminate the coordination constraint by handling both standards programmatically? If so, infrastructure_lock_in may dissolve, reclassifying the mountain as a rope of legacy fleet composition.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) - technology disruption that threatens current beneficiaries of standardization

omegas.description: Is cognitive_handedness_bias a genuine biological constraint or post-hoc rationalization? Deferred axis may warrant generation if ergonomic evidence strengthens.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Four distinct axes pass independence testing with different observables and structural deltas. Coordination mechanism (rope), physical infrastructure (mountain), network effects (rope), and border friction (tangled_rope) form coherent constraint topology.
